channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio e Nossa Senhora: caso vira 3ª maior controvérsia política do ano
item.description: The case involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and the title of patron saint granted to Our Lady of Aparecida became the third-largest political controversy of the year, generating nearly 1 million social media posts. The controversy centers on potential political influence in the decision and revives debates about religion and the state in Brazil.

item.title: Destino de Alexandre de Moraes pode ficar para depois do Carnaval, avaliam ministros
item.description: The fate of Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, investigated for communications with banker Daniel Vorcaro, may only be decided after Carnival 2027 due to the court recess and the October 2026 election context. Justice Flávio Dino requested a review of the case, interrupting the session and making a quick ruling unlikely. Some justices prefer to delay harsh decisions until after the 2026 elections, regardless of whether Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro wins.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro investiu R$ 17,9 mil para impulsionar posts perto do 7/9
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro spent R$ 17,900 to boost social media posts in September, particularly between September 5 and 8, with the highest spending on September 7, linked to pro-Bolsonaro protests. The campaign was connected to ghost profiles spreading misinformation against Lula following the September 7 demonstrations. Flávio Bolsonaro also invested R$ 39,000 in post promotions during a similar timeframe.

item.title: Plantaram Moraes, colheram Mendonça
item.description: The article discusses how insecurity generated by Lula's measures in the final stretch of the first round of elections encouraged his electorate to adopt a radical stance, including the spread of misinformation. Even after GloboNews debunked the information about a supposed evangelical movement to remove the title of patron saint of Brazil from Our Lady of Aparecida, Lula supporters continued to spread the lie.

item.title: Kassio derruba jingle de Lula sobre Flávio Bolsonaro com menções a Vorcaro, Queiroz e miliciano
item.description: TSE president Kassio Nunes Marques suspended a campaign jingle by Lula referencing political scandals involving Flávio Bolsonaro, including mentions of Daniel Vorcaro, Queiroz, and a militia member. The ruling cited that the content exceeded the limits of admissible political-electoral criticism, potentially misleading voters about the current legal status of those involved. Until the TSE plenary rules on the matter, Lula's campaign is barred from airing the contested advertisement.

item.title: TRE suspende distribuição de panfletos e vídeo que associam JHC a Lula
item.description: The electoral judge at TRE-AL suspended the distribution of pamphlets and videos linking gubernatorial candidate JHC to President Lula, claiming it misleads voters into believing in a non-existent political alliance. The coalition led by Renan Filho challenged the legality of using Lula's image in JHC's campaign, as the PT is not part of the PSDB's local coalition. The ruling aims to ensure electoral advertising complies with officially registered alliances.

item.title: 37% avaliam o Congresso como ruim ou péssimo, diz Datafolha
item.description: A September 2026 Datafolha poll shows 37% of voters rate the National Congress as bad or very bad, while only 18% see it as good or excellent. Negative views are higher among men, higher-income individuals, and supporters of both Lula and Bolsonaro, with regional and socioeconomic disparities also noted.

item.title: As cinco forças que podem decidir a eleição (por Gaudêncio Torquato)
item.description: The 2026 presidential election between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro is tied, with high rejection rates for both candidates. Five key forces that could determine the outcome include the anti-system narrative, continuation of social programs, Bolsa Família adjustment, base mobilization, and convincing undecided voters.

item.title: Lula “esquece” região Norte e prioriza o Sudeste no 1º turno
item.description: President Lula prioritized the Southeast in his campaign for the first round, mostly visiting São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Minas Gerais, while neglecting the North, where the PT traditionally struggles. The only pre-election visit to the North was to Manaus in May, outside the electoral period. This strategy reflects a focus on decisive states, such as Minas Gerais, a swing state, rather than traditional PT strongholds.

item.title: Busca pelo Paraguai aumentou com reforma tributária, diz consultoria
item.description: The search for Brazilian companies interested in producing in Paraguay increased with the tax reform discussions and high interest rates in Brazil. Around 100 industries contacted the Frontexa consultancy in 2026, attracted by the lower tax burden and greater predictability in the neighboring country. Since 2007, over 230 Brazilian companies have moved to Paraguay under the maquila regime.

item.title: “Manobra eleitoreira”, diz Renan Santos sobre proibição das bets por Lula
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) labeled as an 'electoral maneuver' Lula's decision to ban online betting on the eve of the first round. Although he supports ending bets, he criticized the timing and form of the government's measure.

item.title: A chance de Caiado fazer campanha para Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado's circle dismissed the possibility of him campaigning for Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round, despite mutual criticisms between the candidates during the electoral race. The decision reflects the strategic positioning of the PSD regarding alliances in the electoral landscape.

item.title: Lula x Bolsonaro: o que diziam as pesquisas a esta altura da eleição de 2022
item.description: One week before the 2026 presidential election, polls show a tight race between President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Compared to 2022, when Lula led voter intention surveys at the end of the campaign, the current dynamic presents different scenarios but remains highly competitive between the two candidates.

item.title: Governo planeja reunião com clubes após proibição das bets
item.description: The federal government schedules a meeting on Tuesday (29) with football clubs and the CBF to discuss the impacts of the provisional decree banning online betting and advertising of betting sites in Brazil. The measure, published on Friday (25), takes effect on October 6th, affecting million-dollar contracts such as those of Flamengo (R$268.5 million/year with Betano) and Fluminense (R$52 million/year with Superbet), generating concern over revenue loss and requests for a transition period.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais mostram a distância entre Lula e Flávio após números da última semana
item.description: Recent polls show Lula ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round, with narrow margins ranging from 1 to 3 percentage points. In second-round scenarios, surveys indicate a technical tie between the two candidates. Voting intentions for other candidates like Augusto Cury and Renan Santos remain low.

item.title: Artigo: ‘A última semana importa’, escreve Felipe Nunes, diretor da Quaest
item.description: Despite tied poll numbers between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, the electorate remains fluid and may shift before October 4th. Indecision persists, particularly in the Southeast, with events like the women-focused policy package and the strategic vote potentially swaying outcomes. The underlying movement between candidates, undecided voters, and null votes indicates that statistical stability does not mean voter immobility.

item.title: A nova pesquisa Datafolha sobre Lula x Flávio Bolsonaro, a 3 dias da eleição
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll projects a technical tie between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the second round, with the president leading numerically at 47% to 45%. The survey, conducted with 2,506 respondents and a margin of error of two percentage points, will be released three days before the 2026 elections.

item.title: Nunes Marques suspende jingle de Lula que liga Flavio Bolsonaro a Vorcaro e rachadinha
item.description: The President of the TSE, Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, provisionally suspended a campaign jingle by Lula that links Flávio Bolsonaro to cases of corruption, the Banco Master, and real estate purchases with cash. The decision was based on suspected electoral disinformation, since the ad may mislead voters by presenting allegations without clarifying their status. Flávio's campaign claimed the ad contained fabricated and manipulated content.

item.title: Conheça os candidatos que disputam o governo estadual em São Paulo
item.description: Six candidates compete for São Paulo's governorship in the 2026 elections, with 34.1 million eligible voters. The first round is on October 4, and the second on October 25, with a possible new vote if no candidate surpasses 50% of valid votes. The candidates listed are Carlos Machado (PCB), Fernando Haddad (PT), Izadora Dias (PCO), Tarcísio (Republicanos), Vera Lúcia (PSTU), and Vivian Mendes (UP).

item.title: Situação do BRB é parecida com a eleição no DF
item.description: The Banco de Brasília (BRB) crisis resembles the electoral uncertainty in the Federal District, where it is debated whether the municipal election will be decided in one or two rounds. Although the Brasília government attempts to generate liquidity by liquidating assets, doubts remain about BRB's feasibility in the first round. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Quaest: Lula vai a 40% no Pará, contra 35% de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A Quaest poll released on September 26, 2026 shows President Lula leading with 40% of voting intentions in Pará, against 35% for Flávio Bolsonaro. Both candidates showed growth compared to the previous survey conducted on August 29, when Lula had 37% and Flávio 29%. The poll interviewed 804 voters between September 22 and 25, with a margin of error of three percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Moraes vai assumir a presidência do STF daqui a um ano?
item.description: Alexandre de Moraes may assume the STF presidency in 2027, if he remains a justice until September 29. The information is part of an exclusive report highlighting the possibility of his swearing-in at the Court.

item.title: A aposta entre aliados de Flávio sobre Caiado
item.description: Supporters of Flávio Bolsonaro consider announcing Ronaldo Caiado as Minister of Public Security in the second round, should the Zero Um candidate win the 2026 elections.

item.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders performam hoje no Rio; conheça líderes de torcidas cariocas que também vivem paixão pelo esporte
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders perform in Rio de Janeiro ahead of the NFL game between the Cowboys and Ravens, highlighting a blend of sports and tourism. The squad of 36 cheerleaders visited Christ the Redeemer and rehearsed at Maracanã, drawing attention from local fans like Juliana Fernandes, a longtime practitioner of the sport. The event underscores the growing interest in American football in Brazil and boosts luxury tourism in the city.

item.title: Depois do STF, celulares de Vorcaro vão causar estragos no STJ
item.description: Content from Daniel Vorcaro's phones, which already affected Supreme Court justices, is expected to significantly impact the Superior Court of Justice (STJ). The material may be disclosed directly to judges or through relatives working in the court.

item.title: Insulto, assédio e ameaça: os casos de violência política de gênero no DF
item.description: In 2026, seven female parliamentary candidates in the Federal District took cases of harassment, threats, and gender-based political violence to the Electoral Justice. The TSE launched the data panel of the 'Political Violence has Gender' action, consolidating information nationwide, with 177 lawsuits and 436 complaints since 2018, mostly involving insults and reputation attacks. The initiative aims to facilitate reporting and protect women in politics from aggressions that impact democracy.

item.title: Pánico moral, furor evangélico y guerra cultural: la fórmula bolsonarista que amenaza a Lula
item.description: The article examines how Jair Bolsonaro leveraged moral panic, evangelical fervor, and cultural wars to mobilize conservative base, attack minorities, and target Lula before the 2018 elections. His polarization strategy and criminalization of opponents threaten democratic stability and the left in Brazil.

item.title: VÍDEO: Como nascem as leis e qual o caminho para aprovação no Congresso?
item.description: The video explains how laws are created in Brazil by outlining the legislative paths of bills, provisional measures, and constitutional amendment proposals. It emphasizes the role of the National Congress in the legislative process and helps citizens understand how governmental institutions function. It is part of a 50-video series aimed at preparing voters for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Jornalistas criticam “GloboNews” por corrigir informação sobre padroeira
item.description: GloboNews corrected a comment by Maria Cristina Fernandes regarding a supposed evangelical movement to remove Our Lady of Aparecida as Brazil's patron saint, clarifying the proposal dated back to 2007 and was archived. Journalists criticized the network for not verifying the information before broadcasting, sparking controversy involving candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula errou em 2023
item.description: In 2022, Lula won a narrow victory over Bolsonaro but interpreted it as a mandate, underestimating the polarization and the need for broader coalitions. This premature reading may have led to strategic missteps in post-election governance.

item.title: Na eleição para deputado, fisiologismo é estratégia, e localismo é projeto
item.description: In the election for state deputy, candidates adopt strategies similar to those of city councilors, leveraging the Brazilian electoral system that combines proportional representation in large districts with open lists. The two basic strategies are either to seek votes spread across the entire state or concentrate them in a few municipalities, highlighting localism as specific projects for each region.

item.title: Câmara dos Deputados concentra funções que moldam leis, gastos e fiscalização
item.description: During the 200th anniversary session of the Chamber of Deputies, Michel Temer emphasized the Legislative branch as the first of the three powers, responsible for shaping laws, budget, and oversight. The speech reinforced the importance of Parliament in the Brazilian democratic structure.

item.title: Conheça livros que analisam as eleições e o cenário político no Brasil
item.description: Recent books examine how income distribution policies, evangelical churches, ideological polarization and social media shape the Brazilian electorate ahead of the 2026 elections. The recommended reading explores the main factors that will influence voting behavior on election day. The collection presents various perspectives on the current political scenario.

item.title: Fake news de Flávio e a padroeira é 3º maior assunto político nas redes
item.description: A fake news involving Flávio Bolsonaro and the alleged intention to remove the title of patron saint of Brazil from Our Lady of Aparecida became the third largest political topic on social media in 2026, with 977.6 thousand publications and 8.5 million interactions. The controversy arose after a statement on GloboNews, was widely refuted by Flávio and corrected by the broadcaster, and led to a ruling by Minister André Mendonça to remove allegedly false content. The left led the reaction with 66% of posts and 70% of interactions.

item.title: Criador de Dilma Bolada nega autoria de fake news sobre Flávio e Nossa Senhora
item.description: Jeferson Monteiro, creator of the Dilma Bolada page, denied authoring a fake news story about Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Our Lady of Aparecida. He said the false news was an attempt to manipulate public debate and emphasized he would never make a false statement.

item.title: Após estimular fake news sobre N.S. Aparecida, coordenador da Secom invoca ‘liberdade de expressão’
item.description: The coordinator of the Presidential Secretariat of Communication (Secom), George Marques da Silva, shared a post that spread a false claim linking Flávio Bolsonaro to a bill archived in 2007. He later justified his action under the banner of freedom of expression. The incident sparked reactions from Lula’s supporters and criticism from those warning against institutional disinformation.

item.title: Financial Times compara os Bolsonaros à família Trump e diz que têm estilo paranoico de política
item.description: The Financial Times published a feature comparing the Bolsonaro family to the Trump family, describing them as a radical clan with a paranoid style of politics. The analysis highlights internal divisions and the possibility of Flávio Bolsonaro consolidating a political dynasty in case of electoral victory. The magazine also contextualizes the importance of the elections for international influence, especially in the US.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio faz live com Padre Kelmon e pai de santo de Anitta
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign held a live stream with religious leaders, including Father Kelmon and pai de santo Sérgio Pina, amid rumors about Brazil's patron saint.

item.title: Aliados de Lula criticam Mendonça por tirar do ar fake news sobre padroeira
item.description: Lula's allies criticized TSE Minister André Mendonça for ordering the removal of posts containing fake news about Flávio Bolsonaro allegedly planning to remove Our Lady of Aparecida as Brazil's patron saint. They deemed the decision censorship and questioned electoral interference.

item.title: A uma semana da eleição, campanhas de Lula e Flávio Bolsoanro tentam alcançar indecisos
item.description: One week before the runoff, the campaigns of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) intensify efforts to win over undecided voters and mobilize their bases amid high polarization and political tension. The final stretch is marked by targeted communication strategies and the need to avoid negative events that could shift the agenda.

item.title: Fake sobre N.S Aparecida tem 1 milhão de posts e vira 3ª maior repercussão do ano nas redes
item.description: A false claim linking senator Flávio Bolsonaro to a bill revoking Nossa Senhora Aparecida as Brazil's patron saint generated 977.6 thousand social media posts in 55 hours, becoming the third biggest political topic of 2026. The misinformation, spread by pro-government influencers, sparked 8.5 million interactions and fueled religious and electoral debates.

item.title: Desaprovação do STF atinge nível máximo no País, aponta pesquisa
item.description: Disapproval of STF ministers reached 47%, the highest in history, according to Datafolha. The increase is linked to revelations of possible connections between ministers and Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Banco Master. Among Lula voters, 32% approve of the STF, while among Flávio Bolsonaro voters, only 6% approve.

item.title: Nunes Marques manda suspender jingle de Lula “foi o Flávio Bolsonaro”
item.description: The president of the TSE, Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, provisionally suspended a campaign jingle by Lula that links Flávio Bolsonaro to corruption schemes, as it contains distorted information and may mislead voters. The minister emphasized that the song's catchy and repetitive format could cause irreversible damage during the electoral period by presenting unproven or already dismissed facts.

item.title: Uma eleição do ‘menos pior’, mas disputada pau a pau
item.description: The 2026 election is portrayed as a tight 'lesser of two evils' race devoid of popular enthusiasm. Both outcomes — a Flávio Bolsonaro or Lula victory — forecast institutional crisis, a weakened executive, STF tensions, and corruption probes targeting candidates' families and allies. Despite political risks, the text underscores Brazil's economic strength driven by agribusiness, renewable energy, and natural resources.

item.title: A dura avaliação dos eleitores sobre o Supremo Tribunal Federal, segundo pesquisa
item.description: Datafolha survey reveals that 47% of Brazilians negatively assess the work of the STF, the worst index in the historical series (2019-2026). Among Lula supporters, 32% view the STF positively; among Flávio Bolsonaro voters, only 6% consider the ministers' work good or excellent, with 69% expressing negative views. Registered with the TSE, the poll also shows 45% of voters support creating an Ethics Code for STF ministers.

item.title: Quaest: Lula atinge 40%, Flávio marca 35% e Cury tem 7% no Pará
item.description: Quaest poll shows Lula leading with 40% of voting intentions in Pará, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro with 35% and Augusto Cury with 7% for the first round. The margin of error is 3 percentage points, with 83% of voters stating their choice is final.

item.title: Zema e Renan dizem que proibição das bets de Lula é medida eleitoreira
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) and Renan Santos (Missão) criticized Lula's MP 1.394/2026 banning bets, calling it an electioneering move before the first round. Both agree online betting harms families but question the electoral timing of the prohibition.

item.title: “Aberração eleitoral”, diz Zema sobre medidas anunciadas por Lula
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) classified the Lula administration's recent measures, including the betting ban, as an 'electoral aberration' and accused the president of political opportunism on the eve of the 2026 election.

item.title: Datafolha: 37% avaliam trabalho do Congresso Nacional como ruim ou péssimo
item.description: Datafolha poll reveals 37% of voters rate Congress as bad or terrible, while 18% see it as excellent or good. Among Lula voters, 22% view Congress positively; among Flávio Bolsonaro voters, only 15% do.

item.title: Quaest no Pará: 47% aprovam e 25% desaprovam governo de Hana Ghassan (MDB)
item.description: A new Quaest poll in Pará shows that 47% of voters approve of Governor Hana Ghassan's (MDB) administration, while 25% disapprove, according to a survey conducted between September 22 and 25. The main concern among voters is healthcare (37%), followed by violence (12%) and infrastructure (7%). The poll had a margin of error of 3 percentage points and a 95% confidence level.
